quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What happens when you ride alongside another rider?

options.text: You use more of the road surface.
You limit your ways to escape if something goes wrong.
You can communicate with the other rider.
Other vehicles can pass you more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You limit your ways to escape if something goes wrong.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle. It limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Move to the edge of the road.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, avoid sudden moves, stay away from the road's edge, and ride in the tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which lane position is best?

options.text: One that gives you less space and lets others see you.
One that gives you more space and lets others see you.
One that exposes you to more hazards and lets others pass you.
One that reduces hazards but requires you to follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that gives you more space and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you the most space around you. This helps you see others, lets them see you, keeps you away from wind gusts and blind spots, prevents others from sharing your lane, and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close while staying safe?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while maintaining safe space between them. Use single-file when in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: How does braking in a turn compare to braking on a straightaway?

options.text: You should use only the front brake.
You should use only the rear brake.

questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must know the correct technique and be very careful.

questions.question: A person drinks seven drinks in three hours. The body removes one drink per hour. How many drinks remain three hours after their last drink?
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours that have passed from the drinks consumed. Seven drinks minus six hours (three hours drinking plus three hours after) equals one drink removed per hour, leaving about four drinks in the system.

questions.question: What lane position should riders use in general?

options.text: Change positions often to avoid boredom.
Choose a position that gives you the most space.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a position that gives you the most space.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change constantly, so the safest lane position also changes. Pick the position that gives you the most space and lets other drivers see you best.

questions.question: What does NOT help reduce injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing reduce injury risk. A windshield does not provide meaningful protection from crash injuries.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Use only your mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
Do not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let vehicles in your blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before. Explain what they need to do.
Not explain anything since they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before. Explain what they need to do.
questions.explanation: A passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Never assume they have ridden before. Give clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: A group of riders should merge onto a highway in:
questions.explanation: Staggered formation is best for normal riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Keep them from leaving until they are sober.

questions.explanation: Stop someone from riding while impaired. You can arrange another way home, involve them in other activities, keep them from leaving before they are sober, and get other friends to help.

questions.question: When riding near stopped or slow cars, a rider should:

options.text: Pull over and wait for traffic to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through quickly.
Weave between cars to get through quickly.

questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors may open or cars may pull out. You won't have room to turn or stop safely. Never ride on the shoulder—other drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: You should do all of the following to reduce your chance of a crash, except:

options.text: Be visible by wearing proper clothing and using your headlight.
Signal your turns and use your brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure you are visible, signal your moves, and look for hazards. Stay prepared to react to anything. Do not rely on hope.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:
questions.explanation: The rear brake is operated by the right foot.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you in turns and curves. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least one hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes after riding starts.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not kick the dog.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Limiting rides to six hours or less per day

questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest. Do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain, as these make you tire faster. Never use artificial stimulants. When they wear off, the effects can be very dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little slower than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, making it sit lower. Ride slower than usual, especially through curves and over bumps. The extra weight means your motorcycle takes longer to speed up, slow down, and stop. You should keep a larger space cushion between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: When going through a turn on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look closely at the front of the motorcycle.
Look through the turn to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the turn to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles can look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge a motorcycle's real location and speed.

questions.question: Crashes are most likely to happen to:

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to untrained, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Clean and adjust both mirrors before starting your motorcycle. Position them so you can see the lane behind you and as much as possible of the lanes next to you.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and show some leg.

questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or strong synthetic material that cover your entire legs. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it restricts your movement.

questions.question: When a rider's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the rider:
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals instead of turn signals to show their plans. When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left, it means they plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
Guarantees the driver will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles and still do not see them.
